column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:matrix-util module
# Loadable module of dense Matrix utilities. Import binds the
# `MatrixUtil` namespace, then words are called via dot-access:
# words build a Matrix (a rank-2 Tensor); a Matrix renders in its
# canonical shape form `Matrix(rowsXcols)`. Numeric results are Floats.
# Note: zeros/ones take (cols rows) in forward order — `zeros 3 2`
# builds a 2x3 matrix. The accessors elem/row/col/scale carry DUAL
# signature orders: the natural matrix-first forward form
# (`MatrixUtil.row m 1`, `MatrixUtil.elem m row col`) and the legacy
# stack form (`(matrix) MatrixUtil.row 1`) both dispatch — the matched

column3: create: build a Matrix from a list of equal-length rows
zeros: an all-zero matrix (forward args are cols then rows)
ones: an all-one matrix
fill: a rowsXcols matrix of a constant value
rows: number of rows
cols: number of columns

column1: # §3  access (matrix read from the stack; indices are forward args)

column3: elem: a single entry — here row 0, col 1 (legacy stack form, col-row order)
row: one row as a list (legacy stack form)
col: one column as a list (legacy stack form)
elem forward form: matrix first, then row col — the wrapper's declared order
row forward form: matrix first
col forward form: matrix first
mat-add: element-wise sum
mat-sub: element-wise difference
mat-mul: matrix product
mat-mul forward form is B·A (operand-order pin: A is 2x3, B is 3x2, so B·A is 3x3 — a square spec row cannot catch a reversal)
mat-mul stack/swap form is A·B (the mirror of the forward row above; A·B is 2x2)
mat-emul: element-wise (Hadamard) product
scale: multiply every entry by a scalar (scalar-first legacy order)
scale forward form: matrix first
transpose: swap rows and columns
values: the row-major flat list of entries
sum: total of all entries
tr: trace (sum of the diagonal)
det: determinant
dot: dot product of two equal-length vectors
`MatrixUtil` is unbound without `import`
create rejects ragged rows
